text: 事了拂衣去，深藏身与名
pinyin: shì liǎo fú yī qù, shēn cáng shēn yǔ míng
literal: task · done · brush · clothes · leave, deeply · hide · self · and · name
natural: once the deed is done, brush off your clothes and go, hiding both body and name

meaning.en: After the deed is done, walk away without seeking reward or fame; said of someone who does good and quietly withdraws.
meaning.zh: 事情办完就拂拂衣袖离去，不求回报，也不留名声；形容做了好事悄然隐退。

equivalents: do good and slip away unnamed
do a good deed and ask for no credit

examples.zh: 他捐了款就走，真是“事了拂衣去，深藏身与名”。
examples.en: He made the donation and left, truly 'once the deed is done, brush off your clothes and go, hiding body and name'.

examples.zh: 老教授退休后不再过问学院的事，事了拂衣去，深藏身与名。
examples.en: After retiring the old professor stopped meddling in the department: the job done, he left without claiming any credit.

story.en: Li Bai's 'Ballad of the Knight-Errant' (《侠客行》) ends with these lines after the knights' feats ('Ten paces, one man slain; a thousand li, no stopping').
story.zh: 李白《侠客行》写侠客“十步杀一人，千里不留行”，结尾即“事了拂衣去，深藏身与名”。

usage.en: Often used to praise quiet benefactors, or humorously for someone who finishes a job and disappears. Literary; it is the closing couplet of Li Bai's martial-chivalry poem, whose heroes kill ten men in ten steps and then vanish.
usage.zh: 常用来称赞默默行善的人，也可戏指做完事就消失的人。书面语；出自李白侠客诗的结尾，诗中侠客十步杀一人，事后悄然隐去。

text: 文章憎命达，魑魅喜人过
pinyin: wén zhāng zēng mìng dá, chī mèi xǐ rén guò
literal: writing · hates · fate · successful, goblins · delight · in people · passing by
natural: good writing hates a smooth fate; mountain demons delight when travellers pass

meaning.en: Du Fu's lines to the exiled Li Bai: fine writers are cursed with hard lives, and malicious forces rejoice when they stumble.
meaning.zh: 杜甫寄给流放中的李白的诗句：有才华的文人往往命运坎坷，而小人恶势力正乐于看他们遭殃。

equivalents: genius is cursed with misfortune
great talent, hard fate

examples.zh: 他才华横溢却一生潦倒，真应了“文章憎命达，魑魅喜人过”。
examples.en: Brilliant yet poor all his life, he bore out 'good writing hates a smooth fate; goblins delight in passers-by'.

examples.zh: 读杜甫“文章憎命达，魑魅喜人过”，不由想起许多怀才不遇的诗人。
examples.en: Reading Du Fu's 'good writing hates a smooth fate, goblins delight in passers-by', one thinks of many neglected poets.

story.en: Du Fu wrote 'Thinking of Li Bai from the Edge of the Sky' (《天末怀李白》) around 759, when Li Bai was exiled and Du Fu, far off in Qinzhou, did not know his fate.
story.zh: 约759年李白流放夜郎，杜甫身在秦州，不知其音讯，遂作《天末怀李白》，诗中有此句。

usage.en: Quoted to lament talented people who suffer misfortune. Literary. 魑魅 are mountain demons that, in legend, waylay travellers; the line is Du Fu's sympathetic address to Li Bai.
usage.zh: 常用来感叹有才者命运不济。书面语。“魑魅”是传说中拦路害人的山精鬼怪；此句是杜甫对李白的同情之语。

text: 冠盖满京华，斯人独憔悴
pinyin: guān gài mǎn jīng huá, sī rén dú qiáo cuì
literal: officials' hats and carriage canopies · fill · the capital, this · man · alone · haggard
natural: the capital is full of grand officials, yet this man alone is worn and wasted

meaning.en: Du Fu on Li Bai: the capital teems with the powerful, but this one man languishes in misery.
meaning.zh: 杜甫写李白：京城里高官显贵满座，唯独这个人憔悴落魄。

equivalents: while the great flourish, one man wastes away
the talented neglected amid the powerful

examples.zh: 同学们个个升职加薪，只有他还在原地打转，真是“冠盖满京华，斯人独憔悴”。
examples.en: His classmates were all promoted and paid more, while he stood still: 'the capital is full of officials, yet this man alone is haggard'.

examples.zh: 冠盖满京华，斯人独憔悴，用来形容怀才不遇的人再合适不过。
examples.en: 'The capital is full of officials, yet this man alone is haggard' suits a neglected talent perfectly.

story.en: Du Fu's second 'Dreaming of Li Bai' poem (《梦李白二首》其二) follows with 'Who says the net of Heaven is wide? In old age he is still entangled.'
story.zh: 杜甫《梦李白二首》其二，下文接“孰云网恢恢，将老身反累”。

usage.en: Used of a person left out in the cold while others prosper; sometimes humorous. Literary. In the poem it is a line of sympathy for the exiled Li Bai.
usage.zh: 用于别人得意而某人落魄之时，有时带戏谑。书面语。原诗是杜甫对流放中的李白表示同情。

text: 君自故乡来，应知故乡事
pinyin: jūn zì gù xiāng lái, yīng zhī gù xiāng shì
literal: you · from · old · home · come, should · know · old · home · matters
natural: you have come from my hometown, so you must know what is happening there

meaning.en: Addressed to someone newly arrived from one's home town: you must know the news from home.
meaning.zh: 对刚从家乡来的人说：你从故乡来，一定知道家乡的情形。

equivalents: you must have news from home
tell me about home

examples.zh: 同乡见面，他开口就问：“君自故乡来，应知故乡事。”
examples.en: Meeting a fellow villager, he began with 'you come from my hometown, so you must know its news'.

examples.zh: 异国的留学生最爱引用“君自故乡来，应知故乡事”。
examples.en: Students abroad love to quote 'you come from my hometown, so you must know its news'.

story.en: Wang Wei's 'Miscellaneous Poems' no. 2 (《杂诗三首》其二) continues: 'The day you came, before my silk window, had the winter plum blossomed yet?'
story.zh: 王维《杂诗三首》其二，下文是“来日绮窗前，寒梅著花未”。

usage.en: Quoted by those far from home when meeting someone from the same place. Literary but easy; the poem goes on to ask only whether the plum tree by the window has bloomed.
usage.zh: 远离家乡的人遇到同乡时常引此句。书面而易懂；诗的后文只问窗前的寒梅开花没有。

text: 因过竹院逢僧话，偷得浮生半日闲
pinyin: yīn guò zhú yuàn féng sēng huà, tōu dé fú shēng bàn rì xián
variants: 因过竹院逢僧话，又得浮生半日闲
literal: because · passing · bamboo · courtyard · meet · monk · chat, steal · gain · floating · life · half · day · leisure
natural: passing a bamboo courtyard I chatted with a monk, and so stole half a day of leisure from this fleeting life

meaning.en: A chat with a monk in a bamboo-shaded temple yard wins the poet half a day's peace from a drifting, busy life; quoted for a stolen break.
meaning.zh: 路过竹院与僧人闲谈，在虚浮忙碌的人生中偷得半天清闲；常用来表示忙里偷闲。

equivalents: steal a half-day's respite from life
a stolen afternoon of peace

examples.zh: 周末关了手机去郊外走走，真是“因过竹院逢僧话，偷得浮生半日闲”。
examples.en: Switching off my phone for a country walk at the weekend, I felt 'passing a bamboo courtyard I chatted with a monk, and stole half a day of leisure'.

examples.zh: 忙完项目，他泡了壶茶，因过竹院逢僧话，偷得浮生半日闲。
examples.en: With the project done he brewed tea: passing a bamboo courtyard I chatted with a monk, stealing half a day of leisure.

story.en: Li She's 'Inscribed on a Monk's Cell at Helin Temple' (《题鹤林寺僧舍》) begins 'All day I drowse as if drunk through spring' and, climbing a hill, he chats with a monk.
story.zh: 李涉《题鹤林寺僧舍》开头写“终日昏昏醉梦间”，因春尽强登山，路过竹院与僧人闲谈而得半日清闲。

usage.en: The popular form (偷得) is a later alteration; the original reads 又得浮生半日闲 and is by Li She (李涉, Tang), though the couplet is often misattributed to Du Mu. People usually quote just 偷得浮生半日闲 for snatching a break. Literary, warm.
usage.zh: 流行的“偷得”是后来的改动，原作是“又得浮生半日闲”，作者为唐代李涉，常被误归杜牧。人们多只引“偷得浮生半日闲”表示忙里偷闲。书面语，语气轻松。

text: 不知江月待何人，但见长江送流水
pinyin: bù zhī jiāng yuè dài hé rén, dàn jiàn cháng jiāng sòng liú shuǐ
literal: not · know · river · moon · wait for · which · person, only · see · Yangtze · send off · flowing · water
natural: I do not know for whom the river moon waits; I only see the Yangtze sending its water away

meaning.en: The poet wonders whom the moon over the river is waiting for, and sees only the great river carrying its waters on: the moon is constant, human life flows by.
meaning.zh: 诗人不知江上的明月在等待谁，只见长江送走滚滚流水；明月永恒，人生如水而逝。

equivalents: the moon waits, the river flows on
who is the moon waiting for?

examples.zh: 站在江边，他轻声念起“不知江月待何人，但见长江送流水”。
examples.en: Standing by the river he softly recited 'I do not know for whom the river moon waits; I only see the Yangtze sending its water away'.

examples.zh: “不知江月待何人，但见长江送流水”写尽了人生短暂与天地永恒的对照。
examples.en: 'I do not know for whom the river moon waits; I only see the Yangtze sending its water away' captures the contrast of brief lives and an everlasting world.

story.en: Zhang Ruoxu (Tang) wrote 'The Spring River on a Flowery Moonlit Night' (《春江花月夜》), a long poem on the river, the moon and the passing of generations.
story.zh: 唐代张若虚作长诗《春江花月夜》，以江、月和人生代代无穷为主题。

date.zh: 唐 · 约7世纪末—8世纪初

usage.en: Quoted for musings on time and the river and moon. Literary. 张若虚's 《春江花月夜》 is so admired that Wen Yiduo called it the 'poem above poems'; only two poems of his survive.
usage.zh: 常在感怀时光、江月时引用。书面语。张若虚《春江花月夜》备受推崇，闻一多称之为“诗中的诗”；他仅存诗两首。

text: 取次花丛懒回顾，半缘修道半缘君
pinyin: qǔ cì huā cóng lǎn huí gù, bàn yuán xiū dào bàn yuán jūn
literal: casually · pass · flowers · cluster · too lazy · look back, half · because · cultivating · the Way · half · because · you
natural: passing through a thicket of flowers I cannot be bothered to look back: half because I follow the Way, half because of you

meaning.en: After loving one woman, the poet no longer glances at any other beauty: partly from spiritual discipline, partly from devotion to her.
meaning.zh: 经历过一段深情后，对其他美人再也无心回顾：一半是为了修道，一半是因为你。

equivalents: no other woman can compare
after you, no one else

examples.zh: 她笑着说，他对别的女孩连看都不看，真是“取次花丛懒回顾，半缘修道半缘君”。
examples.en: She laughed that he never even glanced at other girls: 'passing through the flowers I cannot be bothered to look back, half for the Way, half for you'.

examples.zh: 婚礼上，新郎念起“取次花丛懒回顾，半缘修道半缘君”。
examples.en: At the wedding the groom recited 'passing through the flowers I cannot be bothered to look back; half for the Way, half for you'.

story.en: Yuan Zhen's 'Five Poems of Parting Thoughts' (《离思五首》), no. 4, opens 'Having seen the sea, no water compares; except Wu Mountain, no cloud is a cloud'.
story.zh: 元稹《离思五首》其四，前两句是“曾经沧海难为水，除却巫山不是云”。

usage.en: A favourite line for lasting devotion. Literary. The poem is one of Yuan Zhen's five 'Thoughts of Separation', widely read as mourning his late wife Wei Cong.
usage.zh: 常用来表示感情专一。书面语。此诗是元稹《离思五首》之一，一般认为是悼念亡妻韦丛。

text: 采得百花成蜜后，为谁辛苦为谁甜
pinyin: cǎi dé bǎi huā chéng mì hòu, wèi shéi xīn kǔ wèi shéi tián
literal: gather · obtain · hundred · flowers · become · honey · after, for · whom · toil · for · whom · sweet
natural: after gathering a hundred flowers into honey, for whom is all the toil, for whom the sweetness?

meaning.en: The bee's labour: after all the work of making honey, who benefits? Said of those who toil only to enrich others.
meaning.zh: 蜜蜂辛苦采百花酿成蜜，究竟是为谁辛苦、让谁品尝甜头？比喻劳动成果被别人享用。

equivalents: working for others' benefit
labouring in vain for another's gain

examples.zh: 做了一辈子代工，他常叹“采得百花成蜜后，为谁辛苦为谁甜”。
examples.en: After a lifetime of contract work, he often sighed 'having made honey from a hundred flowers, for whom the toil, for whom the sweetness?'

examples.zh: 老师像蜜蜂一样，采得百花成蜜后，为谁辛苦为谁甜？答案是学生。
examples.en: Teachers are like bees: after making honey from a hundred flowers, for whom the toil and the sweetness? For the students.

story.en: Luo Yin (Tang) wrote 'The Bee' (《蜂》): 'On plains and mountain peaks alike, all the lovely scenery is taken. After making honey from a hundred flowers, for whom the toil, for whom the sweetness?'
story.zh: 唐代罗隐《蜂》：“不论平地与山尖，无限风光尽被占。采得百花成蜜后，为谁辛苦为谁甜。”

usage.en: Used either as a lament (toil that profits others) or, with a positive twist, in praise of teachers and workers who give selflessly. Literary. Luo Yin's poem 《蜂》 is a short satire of those who take everything.
usage.zh: 可作感叹（辛苦为他人作嫁衣），也可反用来赞美无私奉献的教师、劳动者。书面语。罗隐《蜂》本是一首讽刺掠夺者的小诗。

text: 洛阳城里见秋风，欲作家书意万重
pinyin: luò yáng chéng lǐ jiàn qiū fēng, yù zuò jiā shū yì wàn chóng
literal: Luoyang · city · in · see · autumn · wind, want · write · family · letter · thoughts · ten thousand · layers
natural: in Luoyang I see the autumn wind, and as I try to write home my thoughts pile up in layers

meaning.en: Autumn wind in Luoyang stirs the traveller to write home, but he has too much to say.
meaning.zh: 在洛阳见到秋风，想写封家信，心中思绪万千。

equivalents: too much to say in a letter home
autumn stirs homesickness

examples.zh: 秋风一起，他又想起了家乡，念着“洛阳城里见秋风，欲作家书意万重”。
examples.en: When the autumn wind rose he thought of home again, murmuring 'in Luoyang I see the autumn wind, and as I try to write home my thoughts pile up'.

examples.zh: 异乡的第一个秋天，她读着“洛阳城里见秋风，欲作家书意万重”，眼眶湿了。
examples.en: In her first autumn abroad she read 'in Luoyang I see the autumn wind, and as I try to write home my thoughts pile up', and her eyes grew wet.

story.en: Zhang Ji (Tang) wrote 'Autumn Thoughts' (《秋思》); it ends 'Afraid of haste, I could not say it all; as the rider leaves, I open the letter once more.'
story.zh: 唐代张籍《秋思》，末二句为“复恐匆匆说不尽，行人临发又开封”。

usage.en: Quoted on homesickness and autumn. Literary. The poem ends with the traveller opening the letter again at the last moment, fearing he has left something out.
usage.zh: 常用来写思乡与秋意。书面语。诗的后两句写行人临发又拆开信封，担心漏写了什么。

text: 凭君莫话封侯事，一将功成万骨枯
pinyin: píng jūn mò huà fēng hóu shì, yī jiàng gōng chéng wàn gǔ kū
literal: I ask · you · do not · talk · be enfeoffed as marquis · matter, one · general · merit · achieved · ten thousand · bones · wither
natural: please do not speak of earning a marquisate: one general's glory is built on ten thousand dead soldiers' bones

meaning.en: A general's fame is bought with the lives of countless soldiers; a protest against glorifying war.
meaning.zh: 一位将领的功名是用无数士兵的白骨换来的；是对歌颂战功的批判。

equivalents: glory built on a mountain of corpses
the general's fame, the soldiers' graves

examples.zh: 纪念碑前，老兵低声说：“凭君莫话封侯事，一将功成万骨枯。”
examples.en: At the memorial the veteran murmured, 'do not speak of marquisates: one general's glory is built on ten thousand dead soldiers' bones'.

examples.zh: 历史书里写着“凭君莫话封侯事，一将功成万骨枯”，提醒我们别忘了无名士兵。
examples.en: History books quote 'do not speak of earning a marquisate: one general's glory is built on ten thousand dead soldiers' bones', reminding us of the nameless soldiers.

story.en: Cao Song (Tang) wrote 'The Jihai Year' (《己亥岁二首》), no. 1, in 879, during Huang Chao’s rebellion; it begins 'Within the realm lands are battlefields; how can the people enjoy fuel and fodder?'
story.zh: 唐代曹松作《己亥岁二首》（879年，黄巢起义期间），其一开头是“泽国江山入战图，生民何计乐樵苏”。

usage.en: Often quoted in the shortened form 一将功成万骨枯 when a leader's success rests on others' sacrifice, including in business and politics. Literary, critical.
usage.zh: 常简引为“一将功成万骨枯”，指领导者的成功建立在他人牺牲之上，也用于商界、政界。书面语，带批评。

text: 黑云翻墨未遮山，白雨跳珠乱入船
pinyin: hēi yún fān mò wèi zhē shān, bái yǔ tiào zhū luàn rù chuán
literal: black · cloud · overturn · ink · not yet · cover · hills, white · rain · bounce · pearls · wildly · enter · boat
natural: black clouds spill like ink but have not yet hidden the hills; white rain bounces like pearls into the boat

meaning.en: A vivid summer-storm scene on West Lake: ink-black clouds, rain leaping like pearls into the boat.
meaning.zh: 描写西湖夏日暴雨：乌云如泼墨翻滚，却还没遮住山，白色雨点像珍珠般跳进船里。

equivalents: a sudden summer downpour
rain bouncing like pearls

examples.zh: 夏天的雷阵雨来得快，真是“黑云翻墨未遮山，白雨跳珠乱入船”。
examples.en: A summer thunderstorm comes fast: 'black clouds spill like ink but have not yet hidden the hills; white rain bounces like pearls into the boat'.

examples.zh: 作文里引用“黑云翻墨未遮山，白雨跳珠乱入船”，把暴雨写得很生动。
examples.en: Quoting 'black clouds spill like ink...' made the storm in the essay vivid.

origin.source: 苏轼《六月二十七日望湖楼醉书》

story.en: Su Shi wrote this on 27 June 1072 while drinking at Wanghu Tower in Hangzhou; the next lines have the wind sweeping the clouds away and the lake 'like the sky beneath'.
story.zh: 苏轼于1072年六月二十七日在杭州望湖楼饮酒时所作，下文写风卷地忽吹散，望湖楼下水如天。

usage.en: Quoted when describing a sudden rainstorm in writing. Literary; admired for its quick, sharp imagery. In the poem the storm blows away and the lake turns calm 'like a mirror'.
usage.zh: 写作中描写骤雨时常引。书面语；意象迅疾鲜明。原诗后面风卷云散，湖面如镜。

text: 更能消、几番风雨，匆匆春又归去
pinyin: gèng néng xiāo, jǐ fān fēng yǔ, cōng cōng chūn yòu guī qù
literal: still · can · endure, several · rounds of · wind · rain, hurried · spring · again · return · away
natural: how much more can we bear: a few more rounds of wind and rain, and spring has hurried away again

meaning.en: The opening of Xin Qiji's lament: spring is fading under repeated storms, a figure for a failing cause and fleeting time.
meaning.zh: 辛弃疾词的开头：春天在一场场风雨中匆匆离去，借惜春感叹时局衰败、光阴易逝。

equivalents: how much more can we bear?
spring slips away

examples.zh: 暮春时节，她想起“更能消、几番风雨，匆匆春又归去”。
examples.en: In late spring she thought of 'how much more can we bear: a few more rounds of wind and rain, and spring has hurried away again'.

examples.zh: 词里的“更能消、几番风雨，匆匆春又归去”，表面写春，实是忧国。
examples.en: The line 'how much more can we bear: a few more rounds of wind and rain, and spring has hurried away again' seems to be about spring but is really about the state.

origin.source: 辛弃疾《摸鱼儿·更能消几番风雨》

story.en: Xin Qiji wrote this ci in 1179 on being transferred from Hunan, in the Southern Song; the 'spring' is read as the declining dynasty.
story.zh: 辛弃疾于1179年（南宋淳熙六年）自湖北转官湖南时作此词，词中“春”多被读作日渐衰败的国运。

usage.en: Quoted for the passing of spring and, in a deeper reading, for anxiety over the nation. Literary. The text has a pause mark after 消 because it is a ci lyric with its own metre.
usage.zh: 常引以写暮春，深一层则寄托忧国之情。书面语。词有固定句读，故“消”后有顿号。

text: 可惜流年，忧愁风雨，树犹如此
pinyin: kě xī liú nián, yōu chóu fēng yǔ, shù yóu rú cǐ
literal: pity · flowing · years, worry · sorrow · wind · rain, trees · even · like · this
natural: what a pity the years flow by, worn down by worry, wind and rain; even trees are like this

meaning.en: Time slips by, worry and storms wear us down, and even trees grow old; a lament for passing years and an unfulfilled ambition.
meaning.zh: 光阴流逝，忧愁风雨相催，连树木尚且如此衰老；感叹岁月易逝、壮志难酬。

equivalents: even trees grow old
time passes, ambition unfulfilled

examples.zh: 人到中年，他常念起“可惜流年，忧愁风雨，树犹如此”。
examples.en: In middle age he often recalls 'what a pity the years flow by, worn down by worry, wind and rain; even trees are like this'.

examples.zh: 读到“可惜流年，忧愁风雨，树犹如此”，同学们沉默了。
examples.en: On reading 'what a pity the years flow by... even trees are like this', the class fell quiet.

origin.source: 辛弃疾《水龙吟·登建康赏心亭》

story.en: Xin Qiji wrote 'Climbing Shangxin Pavilion in Jiankang' (《水龙吟·登建康赏心亭》) as a northern exile in the south; the line alludes to Huan Wen seeing willows he had planted grown big and sighing 'trees are like this, how can a man bear it' (《世说新语》).
story.zh: 辛弃疾以南归的北方人身份在建康赏心亭作此词；句化用桓温见昔年所种柳树已粗大，叹“木犹如此，人何以堪”（《世说新语·言语》）。

usage.en: Allusion to a line of Huan Wen's (桓温): 'Trees are like this, how can a person bear it?' Literary; quoted for the passing of time and unfulfilled ambition.
usage.zh: 化用桓温“木犹如此，人何以堪”之语。书面语；用于感叹时光流逝、壮志未酬。

text: 却将万字平戎策，换得东家种树书
pinyin: què jiāng wàn zì píng róng cè, huàn dé dōng jiā zhòng shù shū
literal: instead · take · ten thousand · characters · pacify · barbarians · plan, exchange · get · eastern · neighbour · plant · trees · book
natural: I traded my ten-thousand-word plan to pacify the invaders for a neighbour's book on planting trees

meaning.en: A man with a grand plan to retake the north ends up swapping it for a gardening manual: ambition frustrated and put aside.
meaning.zh: 满腹平定外敌的万言策论，最后只换来邻家的种树书；形容壮志未酬、无用武之地。

equivalents: grand plans traded for a gardening book
hero reduced to a gardener

examples.zh: 当年写下万言书的人，如今在家种菜，真是“却将万字平戎策，换得东家种树书”。
examples.en: The man who once wrote the long memorial now grows vegetables at home: 'I traded my ten-thousand-word plan for a neighbour's book on planting trees'.

examples.zh: 辛弃疾“却将万字平戎策，换得东家种树书”的自嘲，里面是满腹不平。
examples.en: Xin Qiji's self-mockery 'I traded my ten-thousand-word plan for a neighbour's book on planting trees' hides deep resentment.

origin.source: 辛弃疾《鹧鸪天·有客慨然谈功名因追念少年时事戏作》

story.en: Xin Qiji (Southern Song) wrote this ci while in retirement, recalling how as a young man he had led his men across the Yangtze to fight the Jin; he ends with the contrast of a failed grand strategy and a farmer's handbook.
story.zh: 辛弃疾退居时作此词，追忆少年时率众南渡抗金的往事，结尾以平戎策与种树书对照，抒壮志未酬之愤。

usage.en: Quoted for talent without a chance to serve, often with self-mockery. Literary. In his ci Xin Qiji recalls his youth of leading a raid on the Jin army; the 'plan' is his proposals to the Southern Song court.
usage.zh: 用于怀才不遇、报国无门，常带自嘲。书面语。词中辛弃疾回忆少年率军突袭金军，“平戎策”指他向南宋朝廷上的建议。

text: 争渡，争渡，惊起一滩鸥鹭
pinyin: zhēng dù, zhēng dù, jīng qǐ yī tān ōu lù
literal: scramble across · scramble across · startle · up · one · sandbank · gulls · egrets
natural: row hard, row hard, and startle a whole sandbank of gulls and egrets

meaning.en: A carefree boat race out of a drunken evening ends with a flock of water birds startled into flight.
meaning.zh: 醉后晚归，奋力划船争着渡过，惊起滩上一群水鸟。

equivalents: a boat dash that startles the birds
carefree, lively and young

examples.zh: 景区门口刻着“争渡，争渡，惊起一滩鸥鹭”，游客都在拍照。
examples.en: The line 'row hard, row hard, and startle a whole sandbank of gulls and egrets' is carved at the entrance and tourists photograph it.

examples.zh: 老师让大家想象“争渡，争渡，惊起一滩鸥鹭”的画面。
examples.en: The teacher asked us to picture the scene of 'row hard, row hard, startling a sandbank of gulls and egrets'.

story.en: Li Qingzhao's 'Like a Dream' (《如梦令》) recalls an evening in a river pavilion, drunk and losing the way home, and rowing into a lotus pond: 'Row hard, row hard...'
story.zh: 李清照《如梦令》回忆溪亭日暮、沉醉不知归路，兴尽晚回舟，误入藕花深处，于是“争渡，争渡”。

usage.en: A famous textbook line from Li Qingzhao's early ci. Said of lively movement and youthful spirit; the repeated 争渡 gives the sense of speed and fun. Literary.
usage.zh: 李清照早期词中的名句，常选入课本。用来描写轻快活泼和少女情怀；叠用“争渡”表现急切、欢快。书面语。

text: 东篱把酒黄昏后，有暗香盈袖
pinyin: dōng lí bǎ jiǔ huáng hūn hòu, yǒu àn xiāng yíng xiù
literal: east · fence · hold · wine · dusk · after, there is · hidden · fragrance · fill · sleeve
natural: drinking by the eastern hedge after dusk, a hidden fragrance fills my sleeves

meaning.en: Drinking among chrysanthemums at the Double Ninth, the poet finds the flowers' faint scent filling her sleeves; the poem goes on to the wistful 'thinner than the yellow flower'.
meaning.zh: 重阳时在东篱边饮酒赏菊，黄昏后菊花的暗香沾满衣袖；词的下文是“人比黄花瘦”。

equivalents: chrysanthemum scent clings to the sleeves
wine at dusk among the chrysanthemums

examples.zh: 重阳那天，诗社的人聚在一起，吟起“东篱把酒黄昏后，有暗香盈袖”。
examples.en: On Double Ninth day the poetry club gathered and recited 'drinking by the eastern hedge after dusk, a hidden fragrance fills my sleeves'.

examples.zh: 她在花前站了很久，想起“东篱把酒黄昏后，有暗香盈袖”。
examples.en: She stood a long time before the flowers, remembering 'drinking by the eastern hedge after dusk, a hidden fragrance fills my sleeves'.

story.en: Li Qingzhao's 'Drunk in the Shade of Flowers' (《醉花阴》, 'Thin mist and thick clouds, a gloomy long day') was written at Double Ninth, and ends 'Don't say it does not break the heart; when the curtain stirs in the west wind, a person is thinner than the yellow flower.'
story.zh: 李清照《醉花阴·薄雾浓云愁永昼》作于重阳，结尾为“莫道不销魂，帘卷西风，人比黄花瘦”。

usage.en: Quoted for chrysanthemum viewing and autumn. Literary. 东篱 recalls Tao Yuanming's 'picking chrysanthemums by the eastern hedge'; the poem is by Li Qingzhao for her husband Zhao Mingcheng while apart.
usage.zh: 常用于赏菊和写秋。书面语。“东篱”暗用陶渊明“采菊东篱下”；此词是李清照在丈夫赵明诚外出时寄给他的。

text: 云中谁寄锦书来，雁字回时，月满西楼
pinyin: yún zhōng shéi jì jǐn shū lái, yàn zì huí shí, yuè mǎn xī lóu
literal: clouds · in · who · send · brocade · letter · come, wild geese · formation · return · when, moon · fills · west · tower
natural: who sends a brocade letter from beyond the clouds? When the geese come back in formation, the moon fills the west tower

meaning.en: The wife waits for word from her absent husband; geese write characters across the sky as moonlight floods the tower.
meaning.zh: 思妇盼望远方丈夫的来信：大雁排成字形飞回时，月光洒满西楼。

equivalents: waiting for a letter by moonlight
who will send news?

examples.zh: 中秋夜，他望着天边飞过的雁阵，念起“云中谁寄锦书来，雁字回时，月满西楼”。
examples.en: On Mid-Autumn night he watched the geese pass and recited 'who sends a brocade letter from beyond the clouds? When the geese come back in formation, the moon fills the west tower'.

examples.zh: 异地恋的她，最喜欢“云中谁寄锦书来，雁字回时，月满西楼”这句。
examples.en: In a long-distance relationship, she likes best the line 'who sends a brocade letter from beyond the clouds?...'

story.en: Li Qingzhao's 'A Sprig of Plum Blossom' (《一剪梅·红藕香残玉簟秋》) is a poem of longing for her husband; it goes on 'the same longing in two places, which no feeling can dispel'.
story.zh: 李清照《一剪梅·红藕香残玉簟秋》写对丈夫的思念，下文有“一种相思，两处闲愁”。

usage.en: Quoted for longing between lovers or spouses. Literary. 锦书 is a love letter; geese were traditional messengers. The poem is Li Qingzhao's 'A Sprig of Plum Blossom'.
usage.zh: 用于写恋人、夫妻的思念。书面语。“锦书”指情书；大雁是传统的信使。出自李清照《一剪梅》。

text: 山盟虽在，锦书难托
pinyin: shān méng suī zài, jǐn shū nán tuō
literal: mountain · oath · though · remains, brocade · letter · hard · to entrust
natural: our oath, firm as the mountains, still stands, but a letter of love cannot be sent

meaning.en: The vow of love endures, but there is no way to send word; the lovers have been parted.
meaning.zh: 海誓山盟还在，却再也无法寄出情书；有情人被拆散。

equivalents: the vow remains, but no letter can reach you
parted lovers, no way to write

examples.zh: 分手多年，他在日记里写下“山盟虽在，锦书难托”。
examples.en: Years after parting, he wrote in his diary 'our oath, firm as the mountains, still stands, but a letter of love cannot be sent'.

examples.zh: 电视剧里，女主角望着旧信，轻声说：“山盟虽在，锦书难托。”
examples.en: In the drama the heroine looks at an old letter and whispers 'the oath still stands, but no letter can be sent'.

story.en: Lu You's 'Phoenix Hairpin' (《钗头凤·红酥手》) ends 'Our oath still stands, but a letter cannot be sent. No, no, no!' Tradition ties it to his encounter with his former wife Tang Wan at Shen Garden in Shaoxing.
story.zh: 陆游《钗头凤·红酥手》结尾为“山盟虽在，锦书难托。莫，莫，莫！”传统说法认为与他在绍兴沈园重遇前妻唐琬有关。

usage.en: Quoted for love lost to circumstance. Literary. In Lu You's 'Phoenix Hairpin' the lovers are reported to be Lu You and his former wife Tang Wan, forced to divorce; the story is traditional, and the exact identification is debated.
usage.zh: 用于有情人被迫分离。书面语。据传陆游《钗头凤》写的是他与被迫离异的前妻唐琬；此说流传已久，但具体所指有争议。

text: 京口瓜洲一水间，钟山只隔数重山
pinyin: jīng kǒu guā zhōu yī shuǐ jiān, zhōng shān zhǐ gé shù chóng shān
literal: Jingkou · Guazhou · one · stretch of water · between, Zhong Mountain · only · separated by · several · layers · mountains
natural: Jingkou and Guazhou are but one stretch of water apart, and Zhong Mountain is only a few ranges beyond

meaning.en: Wang Anshi at Guazhou: the Yangtze is narrow and home in Nanjing is just a few hills away; so near, yet not yet reached.
meaning.zh: 王安石泊船瓜洲：长江只一水之隔，家在钟山，也只隔几重山；近在咫尺，却仍未到家。

equivalents: so near and yet so far
home is just over a few hills

examples.zh: 火车快到家了，他望着窗外念起“京口瓜洲一水间，钟山只隔数重山”。
examples.en: As the train neared home he gazed out and recited 'Jingkou and Guazhou are but one stretch of water apart, and Zhong Mountain only a few ranges beyond'.

examples.zh: 语文课上要背诵“京口瓜洲一水间，钟山只隔数重山”。
examples.en: In Chinese class we have to memorise 'Jingkou and Guazhou are but one stretch of water apart...'

story.en: Wang Anshi wrote 'Mooring at Guazhou' (《泊船瓜洲》) while returning to the capital to take office as chief minister, with his home at Zhong Mountain, Jiangning, just across the river.
story.zh: 王安石《泊船瓜洲》写于奉诏回京复相途中，其家在江宁钟山，隔江相望。

usage.en: A textbook poem. Used for being near home and longing for it. Literary. The next lines are the famous 春风又绿江南岸 ("the spring wind turns the south bank green again") and 明月何时照我还.
usage.zh: 常入选课本。用于离家近而归心似箭。书面语。下文就是名句“春风又绿江南岸，明月何时照我还”。

text: 人生自是有情痴，此恨不关风与月
pinyin: rén shēng zì shì yǒu qíng chī, cǐ hèn bù guān fēng yǔ yuè
literal: human · life · by nature · is · have · feeling · fool, this · regret · not · concerned · wind · and · moon
natural: by nature humans are fools for feeling; this sorrow has nothing to do with the wind and moon

meaning.en: People are born to be lost in feeling; the sorrow of parting is not caused by the scenery but comes from within.
meaning.zh: 人生来就是为情所痴的，离别的愁恨不是风月造成的，而是出自内心。

equivalents: we are born fools for love
the sorrow comes from within

examples.zh: 她常说，人生自是有情痴，此恨不关风与月，感情的事哪里说得清。
examples.en: She often says 'by nature humans are fools for feeling; this sorrow has nothing to do with wind and moon': feelings are hard to explain.

examples.zh: 欧阳修这句“人生自是有情痴，此恨不关风与月”，被许多作家引用。
examples.en: Ouyang Xiu's line 'by nature humans are fools for feeling; this sorrow has nothing to do with wind and moon' is quoted by many writers.

origin.source: 欧阳修《玉楼春·尊前拟把归期说》

story.en: Ouyang Xiu (Northern Song) wrote this ci, 'Before the wine I meant to speak of my return date', on a parting; it ends 'Let us sing the new songs, no need to start the old tune; one song of the old tune cuts the heart in two.'
story.zh: 北宋欧阳修作《玉楼春》，写离别席上，结尾为“离歌且莫翻新阕，一曲能教肠寸结”。

usage.en: Quoted about love, parting and being absorbed in feelings. Literary. Here 痴 means 'obsessed' rather than 'stupid'; the line has a gentle, philosophical tone.
usage.zh: 用于谈情感、离别和痴情。书面语。“痴”在这里指痴迷、执着，而不是愚笨；语气温婉带哲思。

text: 雾失楼台，月迷津渡
pinyin: wù shī lóu tái, yuè mí jīn dù
literal: mist · loses · towers · terraces, moon · is lost at · ferry · crossing
natural: mist swallows the towers, the moon loses the ferry crossing

meaning.en: Misty, moonlit exile scenery in which towers vanish and the ferry is lost in haze; a picture of bewilderment and hopelessness.
meaning.zh: 雾气吞没了楼台，月色也迷失了渡口；写贬谪之人迷茫、前路渺茫的景象。

equivalents: lost in mist
no road ahead

examples.zh: 他望着窗外的大雾，想起了秦观的“雾失楼台，月迷津渡”。
examples.en: Looking at the fog outside, he thought of Qin Guan's 'mist swallows the towers, the moon loses the ferry crossing'.

examples.zh: 那一年他事业低谷，前路茫茫，真是“雾失楼台，月迷津渡”。
examples.en: That year his career hit a low and the road ahead was blurred: 'mist swallows the towers, the moon loses the ferry crossing'.

story.en: Qin Guan (Northern Song) wrote 'Treading on Grass: At an Inn in Chenzhou' (《踏莎行·郴州旅舍》) while demoted and banished south; the lines open the poem, followed by 'The peach-blossom source is nowhere to be found'.
story.zh: 北宋秦观被贬南迁，在郴州旅舍作《踏莎行》，此二句为开篇，下接“桃源望断无寻处”。

usage.en: Quoted for bewilderment or lack of direction, and for misty scenery. Literary. Qin Guan wrote it in exile at Chenzhou; Su Shi admired the poem, especially the couplet 可堪孤馆闭春寒，杜鹃声里斜阳暮.
usage.zh: 用于迷茫无路，也用于写雾景。书面语。苏轼颇欣赏此词；秦观在贬所郴州作此词。
